title: Gravity-sliced canary promotion playbook for private control-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket defines an operational playbook and Terraform/IaC patterns to perform tenant-isolated canary slices for private (VPC) control-plane version upgrades using a gravity-based promotion model. Goal is to enable safe, automated promotion of control-plane versions with tight telemetry gating, automated rollback, and minimal operational overhead for Private deployment customers.

Scope:
- Terraform modules for versioned control-plane resources (operator, webhook, CRDs, RBAC) and an accompanying promotion controller.
- Canary slicing strategy that creates tenant cohorts (slices) with configurable gravity factors to accelerate or slow promotions.
- Health probes and telemetry gating definitions (latency, error rate, reconciliation errors, KV cache hit-rate, model-serving compatibility signals).
- Shadow validation and traffic siphoning hooks (mirroring control-plane API traffic where safe).
- Rollback and quarantine automation with a tenant quarantine arena for forward/rollback testing.

Technical approach and key decisions: 
1) IaC and version pinning: build a reusable Terraform module (private/controlplane_versioned) that provisions a versioned control-plane namespace and associated operator deploymentReplicaSet pinned by imageDigest. The module exposes a `promotion_stage` resource that the promotion controller watches. We chose Terraform because customers already consume our Private modules and it integrates well with policy-as-code checks (Sentinel/OPA).

2) Gravity-sliced cohorts: instead of fixed-percentage ramps, each cohort has a gravity weight computed from tenant signals (traffic volume, SLO sensitivity, security posture). Promotion controller uses weights to compute promotion cadence. Rationale: more reliable tenants with lighter impact receive faster promotion while heavier/newer tenants have slower ramp. This reduces blast radius compared to coarse percentage ramps.

3) Health probes and gating thresholds: define a standard probe bundle for canaries: 
   - Control-plane API p95 latency (target < 120ms, hard threshold 200ms)
   - Reconciliation success rate (target > 99.5%)
   - Operator crashloop frequency (no crashes in 30m window)
   - KV cache warm-up hit-rate (> 60% within first 5 minutes for model-serving control-plane dependent paths)
   - Config-change regression tests (synthetic requests exercising common API paths)
   - Model-compatibility smoke tests for any model-serving operator changes (sampling inference calls against a golden prompt set)
Promotion requires passing all critical gates and no more than a 0.1% absolute increase in customer-facing errors aggregated across cohort.

4) Telemetry and observability: integrate promotion controller with Console telemetry endpoints for fast feedback loops. Each tentative promotion emits a `promotion.attempt` event with a UUID and expected cohort size. We record pre/post histograms and a runbook link. If gating fails, the controller triggers the rollback flow automatically and files a `promotion.failure` event with top contributing signals.

5) Shadow validation and traffic siphon: prior to promotion, traffic mirroring is used where possible to validate behavior without impacting live traffic. For private deployments where mirroring risks exist, we instead run mirrored synthetic requests that exercise identical reconciliation paths and check side-effect safeties.

6) Rollback/quarantine arena: when a canary fails gating, affected tenants are moved into a quarantine namespace where we can run bisect experiments (split half of the cohort back to previous version and half to diagnostic builds). This avoids full rollback and supports faster root-cause. Terraform module includes `quarantine_policy` toggles to isolate telemetry and prevent cross-tenant contamination.

7) Kernel/compatibility matrix: the promotion process consults an embedded compatibility matrix (artifact maintained in the infra repo) for known runtime kernel and driver constraints required by new control-plane versions (e.g., CRI, kubelet flags, operator-sdk compatibility). If incompatibility is detected, promotion is blocked and the runbook points to either a backport or an infra patch.

8) Security and RBAC: as control-plane changes could affect audit behavior, the Terraform module attaches an audit-level toggle and ensures KMS/HSM references are not rotated during canary slices. Security review required for any promotion that touches audit or KMS integrations.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Implement Terraform module `private/controlplane_versioned` with inputs: `version_tag`, `image_digest`, `promotion_policy`, `cohort_weights`, `quarantine_policy`. (ENG task: write module and unit tests)
- Build promotion controller as a small controller (Go) that watches the Terraform promotion resource and orchestrates cohort rollouts using the gravity weights. Controller emits events to Console and triggers synthetic probes.
- Add canary telemetry dashboard template and automated comparison query (pre/post) to Console.
- Add PR template and policy checks so any change to the compatibility matrix requires a two-person review and a security sign-off.
- Write runbooks and add to Confluence and in-repo docs.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs safety: gravity weights add complexity but provide better risk discrimination compared to simple percentage ramps. We will keep the initial feature opt-in for tenants and provide a simple percentage fallback.
- Terraform vs Kubernetes CRDs: we chose Terraform modules for control and auditability in Private deployments; a CRD-based operator-only approach would be faster but harder to integrate with customer IaC workflows.

Open questions / blockers:
- Definition of tenant gravity heuristics (we have a draft scoring rubric but need PM sign-off).
- Exact SLO thresholds for latency and reconciliation vary by customer—do we allow per-tenant overrides? Recommendation: per-tenant override allowed only for non-critical gates, critical gates remain global.
- Integration surface for traffic mirroring in air-gapped environments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module delivered with full unit tests and example usage.
- Promotion controller able to run a staged rollout across 4 cohorts with gravity weights and automated rollback.
- Console dashboard template and `promotion.compare` query available.
- Two private customers have executed a test promotion in staging with no customer-impacting regressions.
- Security review complete and signed off for KMS/audit interactions.

Deliverables and links: see attachments for initial PRs, design doc, and runbook.
